claims.text: Combining non-collinear spin DFT with DFT+DMFT or refined DFT+U will enable computational capture of ferromagnetic ground states.
The proposed approach accurately treats exchange splitting.
The proposed approach accurately treats quantum spin correlations at zero temperature.
Conventional spin-polarized DFT can underestimate or predict zero local magnetic moments in the ground state.
Underestimation or loss of local moments by conventional DFT is especially relevant to elements such as Cr or Ni.
Non-collinear DFT with many-body corrections explicitly captures quantum spin fluctuations at zero temperature.
Non-collinear DFT with many-body corrections explicitly captures exchange interactions at zero temperature.
Quantum spin effects and exchange-correlation interactions are critical under ground-state conditions.
The improved many-body treatment produces detailed non-collinear spin arrangements with enhanced exchange splitting.
Many-body corrections and non-collinear spin treatment better account for quantum fluctuations and exchange-correlation effects than standard DFT.
Quantum fluctuations and exchange-correlation effects are suppressed or inaccurately modeled in standard DFT.
Improved treatment of quantum fluctuations and exchange-correlation effects stabilizes significant local magnetic moments.
Stabilizing significant local magnetic moments stabilizes a ferromagnetic ground state.
The modified approach will predict robust ferromagnetic ordering in the ground state.
The modified approach will predict larger and more accurate local moments than conventional DFT.
Conventional spin-polarized DFT typically underpredicts or misses ferromagnetic ordering because it treats quantum spin effects inadequately.
Success may depend on the parametrization of the many-body corrections.
The proposed method may be limited by computational cost and by applicability to particular material systems.
The quantitative changes in exchange splitting and local-moment magnitude may vary between systems.
